disciplines_applied.assessment: The pool is mostly calm (0.0% decisive). A smooth series can look related to anything, so I size my claims to the sample and do not narrate ripples.

Liquidity is a background condition, not a trigger. An expanding stablecoin supply raises on-chain purchasing power and accompanies risk-on regimes; a contracting supply withdraws it. The transmission to a 15-minute XRP move is long, leaky, and noisy — I claim a tide, never a timer.

USDT and USDC rebalance across chains, so a headline market-cap jump can be plumbing, not fresh fiat. I aggregate the two issuers and read the 24-hour change to separate genuine supply change from internal shuffling.
decisive_frac=0.0% over n=91; scoreboard still warming up (n=83/200). Slow predictors are the classic trap — I demand more proof, not less.
When in doubt I vote HOLD: adopting noise corrupts every forecast it touches, and that is the costliest error I can make.
Pipeline healthy: feed reachable 96.7% of cycles; same market state reproduces the same numbers.

Stablecoin supply is a background condition, not a trade trigger — nobody mints USDT because XRP is about to move in 15 minutes. That is why no APPLY verdict of mine ever skips out-of-sample proof, and why I score this member at the 24h horizon too.
Known: 0.0% decisive reads over 91 cycles. Unknown: whether supply regimes transmit to short-horizon XRP moves at all. Confidence: low — the honest answer for a slow lab.
